result.topic_en: Evaluation of the Dirichlet integral $\int_0^\infty \sin x/x\,dx=\pi/2$ by the double integral $\iint \sin x\, e^{-tx}\,dx\,dt$ taken in both orders, with related integrals, the Fourier integral formula, and a theta-type sum $P_k(t,\lambda)$.
result.transcription:
Math 28 \quad (21) \#8421

Es sei $\omega$ der Werth des Integrals $\int\frac{\sin x.\partial x}{x}$ von $x=0$ bis $x=\infty$
$\Omega$ der Werth des Doppelintegrals $\iint \sin x.e^{-tx}.dx.dt$ von $t=0$ bis $t=\infty$, $x=0$ bis $x=\infty$
Integrirt man zuerst nach $t$ so erhält man
$\frac{\sin x}{x}.dx\,(1-e^{-tx})$
Also $\Omega=\omega$
Integrirt man zuerst nach $x$, so ergibt sich
$\frac{1-(\cos x+t\sin x)e^{-tx}}{1+tt}\,dt$
Also $\Omega=\frac{1}{2}\pi$

Was ist der Werth von
$\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\frac{1-\cos x}{xx}.dx$ ?
nemlich $\int\frac{e^{ix}-e^{-ix}}{2i}.e^{-tx}.dx$
$=\int\frac{e^{-(t-i)x}dx}{2i}-\int\frac{e^{-(t+i)x}dx}{2i}$
$=\frac{e^{-(t-i)x}}{-2i(t-i)}+\frac{e^{-(t+i)x}}{2i(t+i)}$
$=e^{-tx}\left\{\frac{ie^{ix}}{2(t-i)}-\frac{ie^{-ix}}{2(t+i)}\right\}$
$=ie^{-tx}\left\{\frac{\cos x+i\sin x}{2(t-i)}-\frac{\cos x-i\sin x}{2(t+i)}\right\}$
$=-e^{-tx}\left\{\frac{\cos x+t\sin x}{tt+1}\right\}$
Unter Hinzufügung der Constante

Es sei $e^{-\pi}=h$
$\sum_{-\infty}^{+\infty} m\sum_{0}^{k-1} n\;\frac{h^{\frac{tmm}{kk}+2i\pi\left(\frac{m}{k}-\frac{\lambda}{t}\right)[-\frac{\lambda\lambda}{t}-]}}{k}=P_k(t,\lambda)$
$[-P_\infty(t,\lambda)=P(t-]$ \quad $P_\infty(t,\lambda)=P(t,\lambda)$

$fx=\frac{1}{2\pi}\iint_{-\infty}^{+\infty}da.fa\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}dp.\cos p(a-x)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\iint da.dp.fa.e^{i(pa-px)}$

Es ist so auch $\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin kx}{x}.dx=\pm\frac{1}{2}\pi$ je nachdem $k$ positiv / negativ
und deshalb $\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin x\cos gx.dx}{x}=\frac{1}{2}\pi$ / $0$ je nachdem $g<1$ / $g>1$
$\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin x.\sin gx.dx}{x}=\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1+g}{1-g}$ oder $\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{g+1}{g-1}$ je nachdem $g<1$ / $g>1$

methods.what: Dirichlet integral evaluated by interchanging the order of integration in a double integral
Inner integral over t gives the integrand sin x/x
Inner integral over x via the antiderivative of sin x e^{-tx}
Result: the Dirichlet integral equals pi/2
Antiderivative of sin x e^{-tx} obtained using complex exponentials
Definition of a theta-type double sum P_k(t, lambda) with h = e^{-pi}
Sign dependence of the integral of sin kx/x
Discontinuous factor: integral of sin x cos gx/x
Integral of sin x sin gx/x as a logarithm
